dimensions.assessment: Affects the entire United States population, including residents, health care providers, employers, insurance companies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Social Security Act to establish a Medicare for America health program to provide for comprehensive health coverage for all Americans.

dimensions.assessment: Life-changing effects on individuals through comprehensive health benefits, elimination of deductibles, capping out-of-pocket costs, and major operational and financial changes for hospitals, employers, and drug companies.
dimensions.evidence: Medicare for America shall, in accordance with this section, provide coverage for all the benefits, as determined to be medically necessary

dimensions.assessment: Involves massive federal appropriations, new surtaxes, increased payroll and net investment income taxes, excise taxes on tobacco, alcohol, and sugared drinks, and direct price negotiations for prescription drugs.
dimensions.evidence: There is appropriated to the account established under subsection (a), out of any funds in the Treasury not otherwise obligated, such sums as may be necessary

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new title under the Social Security Act, establishes a Prescription Drug and Medical Device Review Board, introduces mandatory nurse staffing ratios, and substantially alters federal and state health programs.
dimensions.evidence: The Social Security Act is amended by adding at the end the following new title: TITLE XXII--MEDICARE FOR AMERICA

dimensions.assessment: Permanent establishment of the Medicare for America program and ongoing tax and regulatory structures with phased implementation beginning in 2026 and 2028.
dimensions.evidence: shall for calendar year 2026 and each subsequent calendar year provide comprehensive health benefits

summary: The Medicare for America Act of 2026 establishes a comprehensive public health insurance program to provide health coverage for all Americans. It creates a transitional public health option for 2028 and 2029, establishes the Medicare for America program with automatic and phased enrollments, phases out existing programs like traditional Medicare, Medicaid, and ACA exchanges over time, implements targeted reforms for Medicare Advantage plans, institutes strict prescription drug pricing regulations and review boards, and introduces various tax provisions to fund the system.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to enroll in Medicare for America and receive comprehensive health coverage with income-based premium subsidies and caps on out-of-pocket expenses.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Residents and Lawfully Present Individuals

affected_groups.effect: Required to either offer a qualifying employer-sponsored health plan meeting specific actuarial and contribution standards or make an 8 percent annual payroll contribution to the Medicare Trust Fund.

Participating providers must accept Medicare for America rates; hospitals are subject to mandatory direct care registered nurse-to-patient staffing ratios and whistleblower protections, and healthcare providers participating in Medicare for America are eligible for student loan forgiveness.

Subject to price negotiations, reviews by the Prescription Drug and Medical Device Price Review Board, bans on excessive pricing, reduced patent terms for violations, and reporting requirements for price increases.
Subject to a 5 percent surtax on adjusted gross income over $500,000, higher Medicare payroll taxes, and increased net investment income taxes.

key_provisions: Establishes a public health insurance program called Medicare for America to provide comprehensive health benefits for U.S. residents and lawfully present individuals, featuring automatic enrollment categories beginning in 2028.

Provides a broad benefits package under Medicare for America including hospital, ambulatory, and emergency services, prescription drugs, dental, vision, hearing, mental health, reproductive health (including abortion), and home- and community-based long-term care.

Prohibits prior authorization and step therapy protocols under Medicare for America and group health plans, and bans private health insurers from selling policies duplicating Medicare for America benefits.

Establishes the Prescription Drug and Medical Device Price Review Board to negotiate drug prices, prohibit excessive prices, issue competitive licenses for manufacturing when negotiations fail, and enforce penalties.

Imposes new tax provisions, including a 5 percent surtax on adjusted gross income exceeding $500,000, an increase in the Medicare payroll tax to 4 percent, an increase in the net investment income tax to 6.9 percent, termination of health savings account deductions, and increased excise taxes on tobacco, alcohol, and sugar-sweetened beverages.
Establishes safe staffing requirements for hospitals, mandating minimum direct care registered nurse-to-patient ratios across various hospital units.
Eliminates the 24-month waiting period for Medicare coverage for individuals with disabilities and removes waiting periods for individuals on State Medicaid waiting lists.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact long-term federal budgetary cost or overall macroeconomic impact estimates are not provided in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Medicare for America Act of 2026 establishes a comprehensive public health insurance program to provide health coverage for all Americans. It creates a transitional public health option for 2028 and 2029, establishes the Medicare for America program with automatic and phased enrollments, phases out existing programs like traditional Medicare, Medicaid, and ACA exchanges over time, implements targeted reforms for Medicare Advantage plans, institutes strict prescription drug pricing regulations and review boards, and introduces various tax provisions to fund the system.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping restructuring of the United States health care system by establishing a universal public health insurance program that eventually replaces existing public programs such as traditional Medicare, Medicaid, and ACA insurance exchanges. It significantly alters federal health policy, corporate health obligations, pharmaceutical pricing mechanisms, hospital staffing regulations, and the federal tax code.
